researchLabel: Why this can help · learning research
evidenceScope: These studies support learning principles. They do not validate Colloquily’s AI grading or prove that one app mode is best for every learner.
spacingTip: After practice: check one gap against your source, explain the corrected idea in your own words, and try recalling it again on a later day.
openReferenceError: Could not open the study. You can copy its DOI link and open it in your browser.
selectionHelp: Choose two or three exams for Multiple subjects, or exactly three for Full colloquium.
single_question_goal: Practise retrieving one idea and explaining why it works. Use this when a concept is new or your explanation is still unclear.
single_question_method: Answer before opening the source. Give the core idea, a reason and an example; then compare the feedback with your material and correct one gap.
single_question_format: One question with feedback after submission. Say your answer aloud if you want oral rehearsal, then type it for evaluation; speech is not assessed.
rapid_practice_goal: Practise giving short, accurate answers across a quick round. Use it to check familiar material; faster answers alone do not demonstrate deeper understanding.
rapid_practice_method: Recall the main idea without notes, add one reason, and read the feedback before continuing. Choose enough time to think accurately.
rapid_practice_format: A short session with feedback after each answer. The time budget is based on up to ten questions; the number you complete depends on your pace.
weak_topic_goal: Revisit questions flagged by past attempts and notice which explanation steps are missing. Treat the score as a starting point for checking your understanding.
weak_topic_method: Try the answer from memory. After evaluation, identify the exact missing idea, verify it in the source, and revisit it on another day.
weak_topic_format: Prioritises questions due for review from previous attempts, then uses the remaining pool. Without prior history, it uses the usual pool. Evaluate the run afterward for feedback.
random_practice_goal: Practise recognising which concept a question needs and recalling it without a predictable order. Select several topics to compare related ideas.
random_practice_method: Before answering, ask: which principle applies here, and why? Compare similar concepts rather than only naming them.
random_practice_format: A mixed selection using your question count and filters, with evaluation afterward. Random ordering can mix topics but does not guarantee deliberate alternation of problem types.
oral_exam_simulation_goal: Rehearse organising an explanation within a time budget: a direct answer, supporting reasoning and a relevant example.
oral_exam_simulation_method: Speak your explanation aloud, then type the answer you want assessed. Review the reasoning after the run, not just how quickly you finished.
oral_exam_simulation_format: Choose a question count and filters. The session budget follows that count and the answer-time setting; evaluate afterward. Timing rehearses the format, and does not itself establish a learning benefit.
subject_simulation_goal: Practise sustaining explanations across questions in one subject and allocating your time. Use it after working through individual concepts.
subject_simulation_method: Answer from memory and make the links between ideas explicit. After evaluation, choose one topic for a slower single-question follow-up.
subject_simulation_format: One timed session using this exam’s configured duration and a sampled question pool, with evaluation afterward. It rehearses the session format, without assessing voice or delivery.
multi_subject_goal: Rehearse moving from one subject’s concepts to another and choosing the relevant vocabulary. Use this for an exam that covers several subjects.
multi_subject_method: At each subject change, reset your explanation around that subject’s core ideas. Review gaps within each subject after the full run.
multi_subject_format: Two or three exams, each in a separate timed block using its configured duration. Evaluate afterward. These subject blocks are not the alternating problem types studied in interleaving research.
full_colloquium_goal: Rehearse pacing and coherent explanations across a complete three-subject session. Use it to find where a longer rehearsal exposes gaps.
full_colloquium_method: Prepare all three subjects first. Answer aloud if useful, submit your written answers, and turn the final feedback into specific topics to revisit.
full_colloquium_format: Exactly three exams. Default: 15 minutes per subject; choose a different duration in setup. Preparation is included. Evaluation starts automatically after all subject blocks finish. This is format rehearsal, not a validated prediction of your real exam grade.
retrieval_text: Recalling material from memory can strengthen later retention. In experiments with prose passages, retrieval practice led to better delayed recall than rereading, although rereading increased confidence.
explanation_title: Self-explanation · connect the why and how
explanation_text: Prompts to explain causal links and conceptual relationships can support learning, according to a meta-analysis. Explain why a step follows and how ideas connect; merely reading an answer aloud is not the same activity.
feedback_title: Formative feedback · identify a next step
feedback_text: Feedback depends on its content and how it is used; a score alone gives little direction. Compare your answer with the goal, identify a specific gap and work on it. Check AI feedback against your course sources.
spacing_title: Distributed practice · return after a delay
spacing_text: A synthesis of verbal-memory studies supports separating learning episodes over time. Useful spacing depends on how long you need to retain the material. A later revisit is the principle; no single interval is best for every task.
interleaving_text: A classroom trial found benefits from mixing mathematics problems requiring different strategies. The evidence is task-dependent: random order is not automatically interleaving, and studying unrelated subjects in blocks does not reproduce that intervention.
timingNote: The session clock includes preparation time. Hiding the countdown does not remove the time limit.
